newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq and Sudan sign oil agreement - papers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq and Sudan sign oil agreement - papers.

text.p: Iraq and Sudan have signed minutes to follow up the implementation of a joint oil agreement, Iraqi newspapers said on Monday.
They said the pact focused on exploration, establishment of refineries and training of Sudanese experts in the Iraqi oil industry.
"Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed and the (visiting) Sudanese Energy and Mining minister Ewadh Ahmed al-Jaz signed the agreement," the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said.

The paper gave no details but said the signing ceremony was attended by the newly appointed chairman of the Military Industrialisation Commission Abdultawab Mulahwaish and Undersecretary of Oil Taha Hamoud.
Jaz met President Saddam Hussein on Saturday and handed him a message from Sudanese leader General Umer Hassan al-Bashir.

Iraq is banned from exporting its oil under United Nations sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Under a deal signed with the U.N. Iraq has been allowed since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise money to satisfy Iraqis' urgent needs.
Sudan sympathised with Iraq in the U.S.-led Gulf War which drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait.
